description: Report priority and placement rules. Applied per node to one log day (24h, project timezone). agent/priority_rules.py evaluates them deterministically, passes the decisions to the report model, and enforces suppressions on the generated Markdown.

guidance: A change-stream getMore with plan COLLSCAN reads the oplog. This is expected behaviour and cannot be improved with an index: never recommend an index for it.
It can still cost CPU and I/O, especially after a restart, failover or consumer outage, when cursors resume from an old resume token and scan a large oplog range.

List it in the findings table and action plan only for a very long scan (max duration >= {long_scan_duration_ms_gte:,} ms or max documents examined >= {long_scan_docs_examined_gte:,}), as {long_priority}. Otherwise describe it in one or two sentences in Query and latency analysis only.

For a listed long scan, say whether it coincides with restart, election or failover events in the extracted timeline. Possible checks: consumer lag and resume behaviour, number of concurrent change-stream cursors, early $match filtering and fullDocument lookup cost (these reduce downstream work but do not remove the oplog scan). Validate by comparing change-stream scan duration after the next restart.

A slow-operation group (change streams excluded) with fewer than {count_lt:,} occurrences in the log day AND an estimated total slow time below {total_duration_ms_lt:,} ms ({total_duration_hours:g} h) is {priority}: probably not a critical index gap.
Still list it in the findings table and the action plan: a new feature or a growing workload can make it significant later.
Estimated total slow time = duration_ms.avg x count, because the extraction has no per-group duration total. Say it is an estimate.
When priority_decisions marks the group new or increased versus n-1/n-8, state it in the row as a watch item.
Groups at or above either threshold are not capped by this rule; prioritize them from the evidence.
Count each type separately for the log day on this node by summing the matching error_scan groups.

Do not recommend raising timeouts or pool sizes. Possible checks: failing users, mechanisms and databases from the redacted samples, recent credential or role changes, misconfigured clients. Validate with the next day's count.
